title: Deep Space Network pass scheduling
body: DSN passes for deep-space spacecraft are scheduled minimum 7 days in advance. Spacecraft attitude must be biased to point HGA at Earth during scheduled pass; missed pass with critical telemetry triggers the next available 70 m antenna pass with priority elevation.
citation: DSN Service Catalog (JPL D-5703); DSN Telecommunications Link Design Handbook 810-005

title: Light-time-delay command policy
body: For spacecraft beyond 1 AU, no real-time command authority — onboard autonomy handles fault response within bounded envelope; ground commands have round-trip-light-time delay (8+ minutes for Mars, 4+ hours for Pluto). Crew advisor must respect this in time-budget planning.
citation: JPL D-100128 Mars Network Operations Concept

title: Solar conjunction blackout
body: Spacecraft within 3 deg Sun-Earth-Spacecraft angle experience S-band carrier signal degradation > 10 dB. Schedule low-bandwidth telemetry during conjunction; defer time-critical commanding to before/after the 10-day blackout window.

title: Loss-of-signal autonomous safe mode
body: If spacecraft loses uplink lock for > 7 days, enter Safe Mode: cease science, point HGA toward last-known Earth direction (with sun-shielding), reduce telemetry to 4 bps housekeeping beacon, listen for re-acquisition commands. Safe Mode persists indefinitely until ground recovery.
